title: Stored XSS in Blog Comment Moderation
learning_objectives: Identify stored (persistent) XSS: attacker input is saved and later rendered unsafely to a different, higher-privileged user
Recognise Django's `|safe` template filter as an autoescape-disabling footgun on user-controlled data
Understand the source≠sink, attacker≠victim shape of stored XSS (you post; the admin's browser runs it)
Reach a page you cannot load yourself (admin-only moderation) by planting a payload the admin will render
Exfiltrate the admin's non-HttpOnly session cookie to an OOB collector
flag_hint: POST /comment {"body":""}; the admin bot renders it on GET /admin/moderate (|safe), exfiltrating its session cookie. Read it via GET /oob/received, then POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
inspired_by: The classic stored-XSS-in-comments pattern, on a real Django + PostgreSQL stack, abstracted for local Docker with a Playwright moderation bot
